title: Use the repo-standard workflow concurrency group, not github.run_id
answers: how should I set concurrency for a GitHub Actions workflow in mlflow
why does my workflow concurrency group never cancel older runs
github.run_id concurrency group is a no-op
pull_request and workflow_dispatch concurrency separation in workflow yml
body:
Convention: workflows in .github/workflows use `concurrency: group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.ref }}` with `cancel-in-progress: true`.
Do not key the group on `${{ github.run_id }}`: every run has a unique id, so the group never shares runs and cancels nothing (a no-op).
`github.event_name` keeps pull_request and workflow_dispatch runs in separate groups; for pull_request, `github.ref` is the PR merge ref, which isolates each PR.
The two Copilot workflows (copilot-code-review.yml, copilot-setup-steps.yml) were moved to this group for consistency with the standard; their path filters make cancellation rare, so the reason is consistency, not runner time.
Constraints: the diff shows only these two files and the PR description calls the group 'repository-standard'; it does not say whether workflows that must serialize (e.g. releases, deploys) should keep cancel-in-progress false, so do not assume this applies there.
applies: Workflow files under .github/workflows in mlflow/mlflow that are triggered by pull_request or workflow_dispatch; not evidence for non-PR serialization workflows.
says: Pushing new commits to a pull request fails to cancel outdated automated review checks.
Older automated code review runs keep finishing instead of stopping on new pushes.
Automatically cancel superseded pull request validation runs when fresh changes are submitted.
Stop duplicate automated check runs from executing concurrently on the same pull request.
search: Workflows in .github/workflows triggered by pull_request or workflow_dispatch must set concurrency group to `${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.ref }}` with `cancel-in-progress: true` rather than keying on `${{ github.run_id }}`. Keying on github.run_id makes concurrency a no-op because each run has a unique identifier, whereas github.event_name separates dispatch from pull requests and github.ref isolates individual PR merge references. This standard was applied to .github/workflows/copilot-code-review.yml and .github/workflows/copilot-setup-steps.yml for consistency, not runner time savings. It applies to pull_request or workflow_dispatch workflows in mlflow/mlflow, with no evidence that workflows requiring serialization such as releases or deploys should use cancel-in-progress.
